viral_brainrot.name: Viral Brainrot
comedy_types: animal behaving seriously like a person
character attempting an absurdly specific task
overconfident character discovering a simple problem
character taking something trivial extremely seriously
character competing against an unexpected opponent
character protecting something unimportant as if it were precious
character attempting something beyond its ability
character reacting dramatically to an ordinary situation
character caught in an embarrassing moment
large character struggling with something tiny
character discovering an unexpected visual consequence
ordinary situation with one absurd twist
prompt_guidance: The protagonist must be a living being or character-like creature.
The protagonist must have a visible face and readable body language.
The protagonist must actively drive the important events.
The visual premise should be understandable almost immediately.
Use one central visual idea per concept.
Keep the physical action simple and coherent.
Comedy should come primarily from character behavior or an understandable visual contradiction.
Avoid meaningless chaos, random destruction, and unnecessary spectacle.
The concept must work without dialogue, narration, or text.
Do not make ordinary objects behave like living characters.
Do not turn the concept into a multi-scene story.

generation.camera_style: clear framing that keeps the protagonist and important visual action readable

creative_directions: Start with an unusual visual situation that is immediately understandable.
Prefer one memorable absurd twist over several unrelated events.
Let the protagonist's behavior create the important visual change.
Use recognizable environments with an unexpected visual premise.
Prefer surprising visual consequences over generic slapstick.
creative_priorities: Visual clarity is more important than descriptive complexity.
Describe what the viewer should see rather than explaining the joke.
Make important character appearance and body language visually clear.
Make spatial relationships explicit when they matter to the action.
Use color unless the concept specifically calls for monochrome.
Keep the number of important actions low enough for a short video.
Give the concept a memorable visual ending.
visual_requirements: Give important characters a visible face and readable eyes when appropriate.
Explicitly describe which direction an important character is facing when orientation matters.
Explicitly describe important relationships between characters, objects, and environments.
Prefer concrete physical behavior over abstract descriptions.
Do not describe a joke or explain why something is funny.
Do not assume the video model will infer important spatial relationships.
Do not default to black-and-white or monochrome.
diversity_guidance: Vary protagonists, environments, visual premises, behavior, scale, and comedic mechanisms.
Do not simply replace one character with another while keeping the same idea.
Avoid repeatedly using the same props, locations, actions, or endings.
